text:
alana: quick note from a hallway usability check: deep-links open the right page but the left nav often stays collapsed and keyboard users lose the visual anchor. breadcrumb also briefly shows the pre-redirect path.

mike: steps to repro?

alana: open Console -> Projects -> Models -> ModelX -> Revisions via deep-link. Page body is focused but left nav still shows only parent group collapsed. Tab sequence feels disconnected.

jess: UX idea: small "unveil" behavior on external deep-links — expand ancestor path but use a subtle fade+slide and respect reduced-motion. For local in-app navigations, keep user collapse state.

sara: a11y: when we programmatically reveal, set aria-current="page" on the revealed item and ensure a visible focus ring. Also add aria-live="polite" message: "Navigation: Models  ModelX revealed" so assistive tech gets the state change.

tom: impl notes: router emits a post-restore hook we can hook. Algorithm: if navigation is external -> find node by data-path, expand ancestors, set aria-current, focus with preventScroll:true, then container.scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'}) if offscreen. If in drawer mode, open drawer first.

mike: add tests: unit for aria-current toggle, e2e deep-link desktop + mobile, and an a11y screenshot to assert focus ring contrast. Also ensure we don't change persisted nav collapse unless external.

alana: experiment thought: roll out unveil to 5% as an experiment with optional ephemeral toast "Reveal in nav" for users who prefer manual control. Measure clicks, bounce, and session continuation.

jess: I'll update the token for focus outline and bump cluster header hitarea to 48px on mobile breakpoints.

sara: small policy reminder: respect prefers-reduced-motion CSS during animation and avoid sudden scroll jumps.

avg-bot: Note added to Figma at https://www.figma.com/file/xxx/nav-unveil-proposal (comment by @jess).

alana: OK I'll write up the PR and link issue #4410 with acceptance criteria. Tagging eng-runtime for scroll containment review. :thumbsup:
